summary: GitHub provides a structured process for registering OAuth apps via developer settings. Developers must adhere to strict rate limits, security practices like protecting client secrets, and specific requirements for public listings, including the GitHub Marketplace Developer Agreement.

reason.text: The registration process involves simple navigation to profile settings and filling out a form for the application details.
reason.label: inferred
reason.note: Model judgement from the verified claims in this guide; not tested.

reason.text: Public listing requires meeting multiple complex criteria including organizational ownership, two-factor authentication, and specific documentation like privacy policies.

go_public.item: Apps must be publicly available and not in public preview or invite only.

claim.text: Apps must be publicly available and not in public preview or invite only.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Apps must be publicly available in GitHub Marketplace and cannot be in public preview or available by invite only.

claim.text: You must enable two-factor authentication for your organization to get publisher verification.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Ensure that Two-factor authentication is enabled for your organization. For more information, see Requiring two-factor authentication in your organization.

claim.text: You must verify your organization's domain to get publisher verification.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Submit a verified domain and ensure that a "Verified" badge displays on your organization's profile page. For related information, see Verifying or approving a domain for your organization.

claim.text: There is a rate limit of ten tokens created per hour.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: There is a limit of ten tokens that are issued per user/application/scope combination, and a rate limit of ten tokens created per hour.

claim.text: Access tokens expire after eight hours.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: The access token expires after eight hours, and the refresh token expires after six months without use.

claim.text: Refresh tokens expire after six months without use.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: The access token expires after eight hours, and the refresh token expires after six months without use.

claim.text: The temporary code for the web application flow expires after 10 minutes.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: The temporary code will expire after 10 minutes.

claim.text: The device flow user code expires after 15 minutes.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: The user must enter a valid code within 15 minutes (or 900 seconds). After 15 minutes, you will need to request a new device authorization code with POST https://github.com/login/device/code.

claim.text: OAuth apps are limited to 2,000 access token requests per hour.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: OAuth apps are subject to a rate limit of 2,000 access token requests per hour. If your application exceeds this limit, further requests to generate new access tokens will be temporarily blocked, and you may receive error responses.

claim.text: The rate limit for an OAuth app using its client ID and secret is 5,000 requests per hour.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: For these requests, the rate limit is 5,000 requests per hour per OAuth app.

claim.text: No more than 2,000 OAuth access token requests per hour are allowed for GitHub Apps and OAuth apps.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Make too many OAuth access token requests in a short period of time. No more than 2,000 OAuth access token requests per hour are allowed for GitHub Apps and OAuth apps.

blockers.issue: Do not use sensitive data such as internal URLs in your OAuth app.
blockers.fix: Only use information you consider public.

claim.text: Do not use sensitive data such as internal URLs in your OAuth app.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Avoid using sensitive data, such as internal URLs, when creating an OAuth app.

blockers.issue: Never include your app's client secret in client-side code or in code that runs on a user…

claim.text: Never include your app's client secret in client-side code or in code that runs on a user device.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Never include your app's client secret in client-side code or in code that runs on a user device. The client secret can be used to generate OAuth access tokens for users who have authorized your app, so you should always keep the client secret secure.

blockers.issue: CORS pre-flight requests are not supported.
blockers.fix: Do not use CORS pre-flight requests.

claim.text: CORS pre-flight requests are not supported.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: CORS pre-flight requests (OPTIONS) are not supported at this time.

blockers.issue: The plain code challenge method is not supported for PKCE.

claim.text: The plain code challenge method is not supported for PKCE.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Must be S256 - the plain code challenge method is not supported.

blockers.issue: If states do not match during the web flow, the process must be aborted.
blockers.fix: Abort the process if the state parameter does not match.

claim.text: If states do not match during the web flow, the process must be aborted.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: If the states don't match, then a third party created the request, and you should abort the process.

blockers.issue: If a refresh token is invalid or expired, you must send the user through the…
blockers.fix: Send the user through the web application flow or device flow again.

claim.text: If a refresh token is invalid or expired, you must send the user through the authorization flow again.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: If the refresh token that you specified is invalid or expired, you will receive a bad_refresh_token error. To resolve this error, send the user through the web application flow or device flow again to get a new access token and refresh token.

blockers.issue: Listings must not actively persuade users away from GitHub.

claim.text: Listings must not actively persuade users away from GitHub.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Listings must not actively persuade users away from GitHub.
